s1.syndrome_frame: Acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: Pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection
key_facts: 58-year-old man
24-hour history of right iliac fossa pain
Nausea and diarrhea
History of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier
Febrile
Hemodynamic and respiratory parameters stable
Abdominal palpation elicited pain in the right lower quadrant
White-blood-cell count of 25,000 cells/mm3 with 85% neutrophils
C-reactive protein level of 180 mg/dL
Abdominal CT scan demonstrated a swollen and thickened tubular structure
Pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

shortlist.label: Stump appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of laparoscopic appendectomy and CT findings of a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection

shortlist.label: Inflamed residual appendiceal stump
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to stump appendicitis and consideration of a remaining stump and abscess on CT

shortlist.label: Cecal diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar right-lower-quadrant presentation and abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Duplicated appendix
shortlist.why_kept: Rare anatomic anomaly that can cause post-appendectomy appendicitis, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Pericecal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: CT findings of a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips, consistent with an abscess

raw.rationale: The patient's history of laparoscopic appendectomy and the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips on the abdominal CT scan support this diagnosis, as stump appendicitis is a known complication of appendectomy.

rejected.label: Inflamed residual appendiceal stump
rejected.why: Although similar, this is not a standard diagnosis term and stump appendicitis is more commonly used to describe this condition.

rejected.label: Cecal diverticulitis
rejected.why: The presence of surgical clips and the specific location of the swollen structure suggest a complication related to the previous appendectomy rather than diverticulitis.

rejected.label: Duplicated appendix
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence provided in the case to support the rare anatomic anomaly of a duplicated appendix.

rejected.label: Pericecal abscess
rejected.why: While a pericecal collection is present, the primary issue appears to be stump appendicitis, which can cause such a collection, rather than the collection being the primary diagnosis itself.
